data.heroTitle: The hidden journey of your Coke Zero can.
data.heroSubtitle: Understanding the lifecycle of this common drink helps reveal its impact on our world.
data.assumptionNote: This journey is based on a typical aluminum beverage can.

chapters.title: From Raw Materials to Can
chapters.text: Producing an aluminum can begins with mining bauxite ore. This ore is then processed into aluminum sheets, which are shaped and filled at bottling plants.
chapters.impactText: Material extraction and processing require significant energy.

chapters.title: Transporting Your Refreshment
chapters.text: After filling, the cans are packaged and transported long distances. Distribution networks move them by trucks and ships to warehouses and retail stores globally.
chapters.impactText: Logistics and transport contribute to carbon emissions.

chapters.title: The Moment of Choice
chapters.text: This small can is often bought for convenience or habit. Its single-use nature makes it easy to consume quickly and then discard, often without much thought.
chapters.impactText: Consumer habits significantly influence product demand.

chapters.title: What Happens Next?
chapters.text: Once empty, your can can be recycled, which saves significant energy. However, if not properly sorted, it likely ends up in landfill, lasting for centuries.
chapters.impactText: Improper disposal leads to lasting waste.

summaryPanel.title: Reflect and Act
summaryPanel.text: Understanding your everyday objects helps empower you to make more mindful decisions.

data.oneSmallChange: Opt for a refillable drink container instead.
